questions.q: The corner points of the feasible region determined by the system of linear constraints are $(0,10),(5,5),(15,15),(0,20)$. Let $z=px+qy$, where $p,q>0$. The relation between $p$ and $q$, so that the maximum $z$ occurs at both points $(15,15)$ and $(0,20)$ is
questions.explanation: Equal $z$ at both points: $15p+15q=0\cdot p+20q \Rightarrow 15p=5q \Rightarrow q=3p$.

questions.q: In Linear Programming Problem (LPP), the objective function $Z=ax+by$ has the same maximum value at two corner points. The number of points at which $Z_{max}$ occurs is
questions.explanation: When the maximum occurs at two corner points, it occurs at every point of the line segment joining them, giving infinitely many optimal points.

questions.q: Consider the following statements: Statement (I): In a LPP, the objective function is always linear. Statement (II): In a LPP, the linear inequalities on variables are called constraints. Which of the following is correct?
options: Statement (I) is true, Statement (II) is true
Statement (I) is true, Statement (II) is false
Statement (I) is false, Statement (II) is true
questions.explanation: Both statements are standard definitions in linear programming and are true.

Corner points of the feasible region for an LPP are (0, 2), (3,0), (6, 0), (6, 8) and (0, 5). Let $z=4x+6y$ be the objective function. The minimum value of $z$ occurs at
options: The mid-point of the line segment joining the points (0, 2) and (3, 0)
Any point on the line segment joining the points (0, 2) and (3, 0)
questions.explanation: $z(0,2)=12$ and $z(3,0)=12$ are equal, so the line $z=12$ is parallel to the edge joining these two corner points; the minimum is attained at every point of that segment.

questions.q: The shaded region in the figure given is the solution of which of the inequations? [Figure: a shaded triangle with vertices A(7,0), B(3,4) and C(0,2), bounded by the line through (0,7) and (7,0) i.e. $x+y=7$, and the line through (-3,0) and (3,4) i.e. $2x-3y+6=0$, lying in the first quadrant]
questions.explanation: Testing the centroid $(10/3, 2)$ of the shaded triangle satisfies $x+y\le7$ and $2x-3y+6\ge0$, along with $x,y\ge0$.

questions.q: A dietician has to develop a special diet using two foods X and Y. Each packet (containing 30 g) of food X contains 12 units of calcium, 4 units of iron, 6 units of cholesterol and 6 units of vitamin A. Each packet of the same quantity of food Y contains 3 units of calcium, 20 units of iron, 4 units of cholesterol and 3 units of vitamin A. The diet requires atleast 240 units of calcium, atleast 460 units of iron and atmost 300 units of cholesterol. The corner points of the feasible region are
questions.explanation: Solving the calcium, iron and cholesterol constraints pairwise gives the feasible region's corner points as (2, 72), (40, 15) and (15, 20), the standard result for this diet LPP.

questions.q: The corner points of the feasible region of an LPP are (0, 2), (3, 0), (6, 0), (6, 8) and (0, 5) then the minimum value of z = 4x + 6y occurs at
questions.explanation: z equals 12 at both (0,2) and (3,0); since the minimum value is attained at two adjacent corner points, it is attained at every point on the segment joining them — infinite number of points.

questions.q: The shaded region is the solution set of the inequalities [graph shows the line 5x+4y=20 through (0,5) and (4,0), with the lines x=6 and y=3, and the shaded region between these boundaries]
questions.explanation: The shaded region lies on the far side of the line 5x+4y=20 from the origin, bounded also by x $\le$ 6 and y $\le$ 3 (as per KEA key).

questions.q: The feasible region of an LPP is shown in the figure [shaded region bounded by the y-axis, the line $x+y=5$, and the ray $x+3y=9$, above both lines]. If $Z=11x+7y$, then the maximum value of Z occurs at
questions.explanation: Solving $x+y=5$ and $x+3y=9$ gives the vertex $(3,2)$, which is the relevant corner point of the shown feasible region.

questions.q: Corner points of the feasible region determined by the system of linear constraints are $(0, 3)$, $(1, 1)$ and $(3, 0)$. Let $z=px+qy$, where $p, q>0$. Condition on p and q so that the minimum of z occurs at $(3, 0)$ and $(1, 1)$ is
questions.explanation: Equal minimum values at both points require $3p=p+q\Rightarrow 2p=q\Rightarrow p=q/2$.

questions.q: The shaded region in the figure is the solution set of the inequations [figure: a triangular shaded region in the first quadrant, bounded above by the segment from (0,4) to (6,0), below by the segment from (0,3) to (10,0), and on the right by the vertical line x=6]
questions.explanation: Testing an interior point of the shaded triangle, e.g. $(5.5,0.5)$, satisfies $4x+5y\ge20$, $3x+10y\le30$ and $x\le6$.

questions.q: The feasible region of an LPP is shown in the figure [triangular shaded region with vertices (0,20), (15,15), (5,5), (0,10)]. If $z=3x+9y$, then the minimum value of z occurs at
questions.explanation: Evaluating $z=3x+9y$ at each corner point, the minimum $z=60$ occurs at $(5,5)$.

questions.q: For the LPP; maximise $z=x+4y$ subject to the constraints $x+2y\leq2$, $x+2y\geq8$, $x,y\geq0$
questions.explanation: The constraints $x+2y\leq2$ and $x+2y\geq8$ contradict each other, so there is no feasible region.

questions.explanation: The line through $(0,5)$ and $(4,0)$ is $5x+4y=20$; the shaded region lies on the outer side of this line, below $y=3$ and left of $x=6$, i.e. $5x+4y\ge20, x\le6, y\le3, x\ge0, y\ge0$.

questions.q: If an LPP admits optimal solution at two consecutive vertices of a feasible region, then
options: the required optimal solution is at the midpoint of the line joining two points.
the optimal solution occurs at every point on the line joining these two points
the LPP under consideration is not solvable
the LPP under consideration must be reconstructed
questions.explanation: When two adjacent vertices give the same optimal value, every point on the segment joining them is also optimal.

questions.q: If $x + y \le 2$, $x \ge 0$, $y \ge 0$ the point at which maximum value of $3x + 2y$ attained will be
questions.explanation: Checking corner points of the feasible region, $3x+2y$ is largest at (2,0), giving value 6.
